Whether the API design (SurrogateType, contractless default for external types) is the right answer to the issue, which also asks for Union and other attribute-driven settings (Product/API design decision with permanent public surface; the issue proposes three alternatives and the change picks a fourth (surrogate type).)
Security/trust implications of generating formatters that access members of external types (e.g. non-public members) (Not examined in this scoped review.)

Full acceptance and compatibility review of the external formatter feature (This is a scoped review. The placeholder requirement contains only a broad feature statement; I did not comprehensively review all generator paths, API compatibility, or serialization contracts. The supplied facts also record a public API check failure, analyzer warning, and missing solution membership for the new test project.)

Generated output of FormatterTemplate.cs and StringKeyFormatterTemplate.cs (The two generated template .cs files were listed as changed but their contents/diffs were not provided, so the exact generated formatter class text could not be inspected directly; behavior was verified through the passing execution tests instead.)

Security review of serializing externally defined types via generated formatters (No runtime deserialization code was changed by this branch, but the library deserializes untrusted input and this feature lets formats be generated for types the reviewer cannot inspect; a formal security judgement is beyond the provided evidence.)

requirements.text: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

claude.basis: The feature is new and absent on base (the runtime tests don't compile with the source reverted; tests.execution_fail_without_fix pass). Under SDK 9 the 7 execution tests pass: a consuming assembly declares [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial formatters for types in a test assembly that deliberately doesn't reference MessagePack (the issue's Project A scenario), and they round-trip and register in the generated resolver. This covers the clause as written. It does not cover everything the issue discusses (Union and other attribute-driven settings for external types), which I refuse below.
